sections.h2: Where does a Portage house sale begin?
sections.html:
Portage sellers deal with three offices: the city for permits and property tax bills, the Kalamazoo County Register of Deeds for the deed, and the county treasurer for the tax certificate that has to be on a warranty deed. Listing with an agent or selling straight to a buyer changes none of that.

Portage sits in Kalamazoo County and is the smaller of the two main cities in the Kalamazoo-Portage metro area. The area was settled in 1830 and Portage became a city in 1963. Several things set it apart from a typical Michigan suburb: two lakes in the southeast corner, a very large pharmaceutical plant, and a tornado in May 2024 that cut across town from one side to the other.

sections.h2: How many people live in Portage, and how do they live?
sections.html:
Portage is a wide city: 32.29 square miles of land hold roughly 1,514 people per square mile. Federal estimates for July 1, 2025 count 49,862 residents, a 2.0 percent gain over the April 2020 base of 48,882.

Few households move in a given year: 86.8 percent of residents had the same address twelve months earlier. College degrees are common too, held by 47.9 percent of adults over 25, so expect buyers to compare listings carefully.

sections.h2: What do Portage buyers ask about the lakes and schools?
sections.html:
Buyers who search Portage often start with the water. Austin Lake lies in the southeast part of the city, named for a settler who arrived from New York in 1833, and West Lake sits right beside it with Portage Road running between the two. Houses on or near the lakes are a separate segment from the subdivisions farther north and west.

School district is the other common question, because the city is split. Most of Portage belongs to Portage Public Schools, while smaller areas fall in Comstock Public Schools, Vicksburg Community Schools and Schoolcraft Community Schools. Name the district in your listing, because a parcel's district follows the district boundary and the city on the mailing address says nothing about it.

Average travel to work is 19.7 minutes, and two large employers anchor the local job market:

  • Pfizer runs its largest manufacturing facility in Portage, on about 1,300 acres.
  • Stryker has been headquartered in Portage since 2023 and operates several manufacturing sites in the city.
  • Kalamazoo, the larger of the two main cities in the metro area, supplies much of the rest of the job base.

sections.h2: What did the May 2024 tornado change for Portage sellers?
sections.html:
The tornado that struck Portage on May 7, 2024 was rated high-end EF2, and reports after the storm counted more than 500 damaged buildings, 60 of them destroyed. The city set up a tornado recovery page for residents and businesses, and the damage path is still the first thing some out-of-town buyers ask about.

Did the storm touch your house? Gather the permits, contractor invoices and insurance paperwork into one folder, because even a buyer paying cash wants to know which roof, siding or windows are new. For a house still awaiting repairs, say so early and weigh selling without repairs against paying for a rebuild. Permits for construction work go through the Portage Department of Community Development, and the Treasury Office collects the permit fees.

The city's recovery page also lists nonprofit disaster case management for people affected by the storm, which can help with insurance and housing questions while you decide whether to sell. Ask the city manager's office for current contacts, since program details change over time.

sections.h2: What fees does the Kalamazoo County Register of Deeds charge?
sections.html:
Recording one deed in Kalamazoo County costs a flat $30.00, with another $3.00 for each additional instrument a document assigns or discharges. Payment can be cash, check, money order, debit or credit card.

Before recording, a warranty deed, a deed with a covenant of warranty, a land contract or a master deed must carry the county treasurer's tax certificate. It runs $5.00 for up to 20 tax ID numbers and $0.20 for every description beyond that. A separate $10.00 city certificate applies only to parcels inside the City of Kalamazoo, which excludes Portage.

Transfer tax is figured on the price stated in the deed, rounded up to the next $500 step. The county's fee page prints $1.10 per thousand dollars for the county share and $7.50 per thousand dollars for the state share. Michigan's transfer tax act (MCL 207.523) makes the grantor liable, so put that line in your net proceeds estimate and get the exact figure from the title company.

sections.h2: How does the Portage tax calendar affect a seller?
sections.html:
The city collects in two installments. Summer bills open August 1 and are due September 14, and winter bills open December 1 and are due February 14. Each bill covers the full January 1 to December 31 tax year, and a deadline on a weekend rolls to Monday.

  • Balances still open on March 1 pass to the Kalamazoo County Treasury, which adds its own interest and penalties.
  • Special assessments for water, sewer and city street work are billed in July with an August 31 due date, so check for an open installment on the parcel.
  • A lender or escrow agent can request a tax listing from the city after the first bills go out.

For a rough view of the buyer's bill, the city points to the State of Michigan Property Tax Estimator, where future owners enter the state equalized value and current owners enter the taxable value. The Portage assessor's office also has a property record form that corrects square footage, bedroom counts and similar facts. Fix any errors before a buyer's appraiser pulls the record.

sections.h2: What if tenants live in the Portage house?
sections.html:
A tenant can stay through closing or move out first, and the lease together with your notice rights sets the timing.

Since late 2025 the city has also run a rental listing website for landlords, with free listings for owners of fewer than 20 units. A buyer who plans to keep renting may take over the lease as written, which saves you the search for a new tenant. Ask the city's Community Development office which local rules apply to your rental, and bring the current lease to every showing.

faqs.q: What will recording a Portage deed cost?
faqs.a: A flat $30.00 for the deed at the Kalamazoo County Register of Deeds. A warranty deed also needs a treasurer tax certificate at $5.00, which covers up to 20 tax ID numbers.

faqs.q: Does the buyer or the seller owe transfer tax in Portage?
faqs.a: The seller owes it. The statute names the grantor, and the county fee page lists $1.10 and $7.50 per thousand dollars for the two shares.

faqs.q: What are the Portage tax deadlines?
faqs.a: September 14 for the summer bill and February 14 for the winter bill. Weekend dates roll to Monday, and open balances pass to the county on March 1.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Portage house damaged in the 2024 tornado?
faqs.a: Yes. Reports counted over 500 damaged buildings after May 7, 2024, and an unrepaired house sells at a price that reflects the work. Keep permits and insurance records for any repairs.

faqs.q: Which district teaches children from my Portage address?
faqs.a: Usually Portage Public Schools, though some parcels belong to Comstock, Vicksburg or Schoolcraft. Confirm with the district before you print it in a listing.
